name: Caro-Kann Defense
summary: A solid, resilient answer to 1.e4. Black prepares ...d5 with ...c6, so the center can be challenged without shutting in the light-squared bishop the way the French does. You get a sound pawn structure and good endgames, plus clear plans against every White setup.

chunks.title: Introduction & Core Idea
chunks.summary: 1...c6 prepares 2...d5. If White trades or pushes, Black's light-squared bishop usually gets out to f5 or g4 before ...e6 locks it in.
keyIdeas: ...c6 supports ...d5, so after exd5 Black recaptures with a pawn and keeps a central pawn.
Develop the c8 bishop outside the chain (...Bf5 or ...Bg4) before playing ...e6.
Against quiet systems like the Two Knights, ...Bg4 pins the f3 knight and fights for e5 and d4.

line.note: Prepares ...d5 with pawn support.
White takes the full center.
The challenge. The e4 pawn is attacked, and White has to choose a system.
Defends e4. This leads to the Classical or Main Line.
Now Black's bishop heads for f5.

questions.prompt: You're Black. Answer 1.e4 with the Caro-Kann.
questions.hint: A quiet pawn move that prepares ...d5.
questions.explanation: 1...c6 prepares ...d5 with pawn support. It is the defining move of the Caro-Kann.

questions.prompt: White builds the classical center. Strike back.
questions.explanation: 2...d5 attacks e4. If exd5, the c6 pawn recaptures and Black keeps a central pawn.

questions.prompt: The Two Knights Variation. Develop your problem bishop actively.
questions.explanation: 3...Bg4 develops the light-squared bishop with a pin, before ...e6. Black is happy to swap it for the f3 knight.

chunks.title: Classical Variation (4...Bf5)
chunks.summary: After 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4, Black develops ...Bf5 with tempo. White chases the bishop with Ng3 and h4–h5, and Black has to know the precise retreats.
keyIdeas: 4...Bf5 hits the e4 knight with tempo, and the bishop gets outside the pawn chain.
After Ng3, retreat to g6 so the bishop stays on the b1–h7 diagonal.
Answer h4 with ...h6 so the bishop has an escape square on h7. After h5, retreat ...Bh7.

line.note: Develops with tempo on the knight.
The knight steps aside and hits the bishop again.
Stays on the active diagonal.
Threatens h5 to trap the bishop.
Gives the bishop the h7 square.
Stops Ne5 and prepares ...Ngf6.
White offers a bishop trade, which helps Black.
A solid structure. Black plans ...Ngf6, ...Be7 or ...Qc7, and castles queenside.

questions.prompt: The knight sits on e4. Develop with tempo.
questions.hint: Your light-squared bishop can attack the knight.
questions.explanation: 4...Bf5 is the Classical. The bishop develops outside the chain and hits the e4 knight.

questions.prompt: The knight hits your bishop. Where does it go?
questions.explanation: 5...Bg6 keeps the bishop on the b1–h7 diagonal, where it can trade off White's best bishop later.

questions.prompt: h5 hits your bishop again. Find the safe square.
questions.explanation: 8...Bh7. The square you made with ...h6 keeps the bishop safe. Next comes Bd3 Bxd3 and Qxd3 e6.

chunks.title: Advance Variation
chunks.summary: White grabs space with 3.e5. Black develops ...Bf5 first, then plays ...e6 and the thematic ...c5 to hit the base of White's d4 pawn.
keyIdeas: The bishop comes out to f5 before ...e6. That is the Caro-Kann's edge over the French.
...c5 attacks the base of the chain on d4. Black often spends two moves with the c-pawn, and that's fine.
Against the aggressive g4 lines, keep the bishop on the b1–h7 diagonal with ...Bg6. Avoid ...Be4 if Nxe4 is possible.

line.note: The Advance. White gains space and cramps Black's kingside.
Bishop out first.
The Short system. Quiet and flexible.
Hits d4. Black's c-pawn has moved twice, but the timing is right.
Supports d4 and invites ...cxd4.
Heads for c6 or g6. This is a standard, balanced position.

questions.prompt: White pushed to e5. Activate your key piece before ...e6.
questions.hint: The light-squared bishop wants to be outside the chain.
questions.explanation: 3...Bf5 develops the bishop before ...e6 shuts it in. That is the main idea of the Caro-Kann.

questions.prompt: The bishop is out. Now build your pawn chain.
questions.hint: Support d5 and open your dark-squared bishop.
questions.explanation: 4...e6 supports d5 and opens the f8 bishop. The c8 bishop is already outside, so nothing gets shut in.

questions.prompt: Find the thematic pawn break against White's chain.
questions.hint: Attack the base of the chain on d4.
questions.explanation: 5...c5! hits d4, the base of White's chain. Spending a second move with the c-pawn is fine because White's setup is slow.

chunks.title: Exchange Variation
chunks.summary: 3.exd5 cxd5 gives a symmetrical structure, and with 4.Bd3 and c3 White sets up a reversed Carlsbad. Black develops actively, and ...Bg4 is the key idea.
keyIdeas: Always recapture toward the center with ...cxd5.
...Nc6 puts pressure on d4 and gets ready for ...Bg4.
...Bg4 develops the light-squared bishop actively, usually aiming to trade it for White's f3 knight.

line.note: The pawn structure is symmetrical, with open c- and e-files.
Stops ...Bf5.
Pressure on d4.
A reversed Carlsbad structure for White.
Active development, ready to take on f3 or pin it.

questions.prompt: White exchanged on d5. Recapture correctly.
questions.hint: This is why the c-pawn is on c6.
questions.explanation: 3...cxd5. Black keeps a strong central pawn, and the c-file opens up for Black's major pieces.

questions.prompt: Bd3 stops ...Bf5. Develop with pressure on the center.
questions.hint: Your queenside knight can eye d4.
questions.explanation: 4...Nc6 adds pressure to d4 and keeps the ...Bg4 plan open.

questions.prompt: Find the active square for your light-squared bishop.
questions.hint: f5 is covered by the d3 bishop. Try the other diagonal.
questions.explanation: 6...Bg4! develops actively. Black's bishop is now better than its counterpart, and White often spends a tempo on Qb3, hitting b7.

chunks.title: Panov–Botvinnik Attack
chunks.summary: With 4.c4, White accepts an isolated d-pawn in return for fast piece play. Black blockades on d5 and develops calmly.
keyIdeas: Pressure on d5 comes right away, so ...Nf6 is essential.
...e6 and ...Be7 give a solid setup. Black later blockades the isolated pawn on d5.
After cxd5, retake with the knight. It is the ideal blockader on d5.

line.note: The Panov. White heads for active, open positions.
Solid. Black is happy to give White an isolated queen's pawn.
The knight blockades on d5. White has an isolated d-pawn.

questions.prompt: White hits d5 again with the c-pawn. Defend actively.
questions.hint: Develop a piece that guards d5.
questions.explanation: 4...Nf6 develops and defends d5. That's the main line.

questions.prompt: Choose the solid move that supports d5 and opens your bishop.
questions.hint: A pawn move that backs up d5.
questions.explanation: 5...e6 is the safest line. Black heads for a standard isolated-queen's-pawn position.

questions.prompt: White took on d5. Recapture with the right piece.
questions.hint: Put a piece on the blockading square.
questions.explanation: 7...Nxd5 leaves White with an isolated d-pawn and puts a knight on the perfect blockading square.

chunks.title: Traps to Avoid
chunks.summary: Three classic Caro-Kann mistakes: a smothered mate on d6, a bishop trapped by h4–h5, and a bishop swapped off badly on e4.
keyIdeas: With a queen on e2 and your e-pawn on e7, ...Ngf6?? lets Nd6 deliver smothered mate.
When White pushes h4, make room for the bishop with ...h6 or block with ...h5.
Don't put the bishop on e4 where a knight can take it. After Nxe4 dxe4 you've given up your best minor piece and kept a weak e4 pawn.

line.note: The Karpov system. It is solid, but there is one trap to know.
A trap. 5...Ngf6?? 6.Nd6# is smothered mate.
Correct. The d7 knight goes to f6, which keeps d7 free for the king.

questions.prompt: White's queen is on e2 and your e7 pawn is pinned. Develop without walking into mate.
questions.hint: Which knight should go to f6? Keep d7 free for your king.
questions.explanation: 5...Ndf6! After 5...Ngf6?? 6.Nd6# it's smothered mate: e7 is pinned and the king has no squares.

questions.prompt: White threatens h5 to trap your bishop. Stop it.
questions.hint: Make an escape square for the bishop.
questions.explanation: 6...h6 opens up h7 for the bishop. 6...h5 is also playable. Ignoring the threat loses the bishop to h5.

questions.prompt: White lunges with g4. Where must the bishop go?
questions.hint: e4 looks tempting, but the c3 knight covers it.
questions.explanation: 5...Bg6 stays on the b1–h7 diagonal, and ...c5 comes next. 5...Be4? 6.Nxe4 dxe4 gives up Black's best minor piece and leaves a weak pawn on e4.
